question: At a fixed 500-Memory corpus and fixed task/query, does matched-candidate density impair useful Memory use, and how strongly does ordinary PageRank's benefit over key order depend on reference-link richness once navigation is available?

scope.ordering_question: Compare key, ordinary PageRank, and same-candidate BM25F without changing lexical membership within a variant.
scope.density_question: Compare nested candidate sets of 10, 40, and 150 while holding task, query, primary Memory, acceptable entry points, corpus size, model, prompt, and ordering policy fixed.
scope.linkage_question: Compare sparse, native, and enriched reference graphs while holding Memory identity/content, candidate membership, task, query, and model fixed.
scope.not_candidate_generation: The primary Memory remains a literal candidate by construction. Literal-matcher recall is tracked separately in mem-lbuvd.

task_design.base_tasks: All 21 frozen held-out tasks from the seven-family structural follow-up.
task_design.independent_unit: base task within graph family; density and linkage cells are repeated measures, not additional independent tasks
task_design.candidate_recipe: Keep the frozen primary and acceptable entry points. Select distractors deterministically by frozen original-label order followed by SHA-256(task_id, Memory ID). Remove the exact query phrase from nonselected Memories and add the same bounded historical-guidance surface to selected new distractors.
task_design.reuse_warning: The task semantics were used in the prior ordering study. Only the newly frozen density/linkage contrasts are confirmatory; this is not an independent fresh-task replication.

linkage_levels.sparse: Preserve each frozen shortest acceptable-entry-to-primary path, when one exists, plus a deterministic 25% SHA-256 sample of all other native edges.
linkage_levels.native: Use the frozen authored reference graph unchanged.
linkage_levels.enriched: Use every native edge and add the reciprocal backlink for every native edge, with duplicates and self-links removed.
invariants: The sparse graph is a subset of the native graph.
The native graph is a subset of the enriched graph.
Existing entry-to-primary reachability is preserved in sparse.
An originally unlinked primary is not given an answer-specific edge.
Memory content and lexical candidate membership do not change across linkage levels.

agent_matrix.position_control: control-semantic places the primary first and acceptable entries next; run only with unbounded visibility to isolate candidate-ingestion load from burial
agent_matrix.targeted_repeat_rule: Add two repeats only for infrastructure failure, policy task-success disagreement, density endpoint disagreement, or an interaction confidence interval touching a decision threshold.

rank_computation.boundary: This is the algebraically equivalent linear-time dangling-mass implementation already differentially checked by the follow-up harness; ranks are derived fixture data and are never persisted as Memory state.

density: task_success under unbounded primary-first position control
linkage: PageRank minus key page-one useful probability
PageRank minus key pages and compact tokens to first useful
PageRank minus key task success under navigation
graph hops, recalls, branching, and navigation reachability
ranking_increment: BM25F minus PageRank cost and success at each density/linkage level

candidate_density_material.rule: Call candidate density behaviorally material only if the paired 90% task-clustered interval clears either threshold under the unbounded primary-first control. Token growth alone is an ingestion-cost result, not a reasoning-failure result.

structural_benefit_link_dependent.rule: Call PageRank materially link-dependent only if its paired advantage over key changes from sparse to enriched by one registered threshold under navigation without a greater-than-five-point task-success regression.

structural_default.rule: Do not make structural order a default if it clears the benefit threshold only in enriched graphs or has a severe graph-family tail. In that case retain it as an optional derived strategy gated by observed graph coverage.

query_specific_ownership.rule: The prior consumer-side BM25F boundary changes only if BM25F clears a registered cost threshold over PageRank in realistic native/enriched navigation cells, especially at 150 candidates.

interaction_contrasts: enriched minus sparse change in each policy contrast

sequence: Freeze the variant manifest and hashes.
Validate deterministic candidate nesting, candidate/projection parity, link-set nesting, reachability preservation, and rank permutations.
Run the complete deterministic oracle grid.
Analyze and amend the issue package without mixing these results into candidate-generation claims.
out_of_scope: literal versus FTS or semantic candidate generation
production Beads schema or search-index changes
claiming that raw link count alone measures link quality
treating transformed variants as independent new task families
